scope_note: Mechanism-level prior-art taxonomy. Subtraction is used only as an algebraic residue/collision detector, never as additive number-line locality.

mechanisms.ambient_carrier: unit group (Z/NZ)^* with hidden projections to F_p^* and F_q^* for squarefree N=pq
mechanisms.hidden_channel_invariant: channel exponent/order dividing p-1 or q-1; stage-1 success is controlled by smoothness/divisibility of a prime factor minus one
mechanisms.public_factor_blind_action: choose public base a and exponent M, compute a^M mod N
mechanisms.collapse: a^M = 1 mod p while a^M != 1 mod q (or vice versa)
mechanisms.crt_restatement: Exact: if p divides a^M-1 and q does not, then gcd(a^M-1,N)=p. The public exponentiation is identical before hidden CRT projection; only the channel orders differ.
mechanisms.success_regime: Classical stage-1 target: p-1 sufficiently smooth/divides the chosen exponent M, with the other channel not simultaneously annihilated.
mechanisms.cost_regime: Conditional on the smoothness bound/exponent construction; this ledger makes no unconditional polynomial-time claim.
mechanisms.bridge_class: one-sided order annihilation -> nonunit witness -> gcd endpoint
mechanisms.novelty_guard_effect: Any candidate reducible to hidden-channel order annihilation followed by gcd is at most a reformulation/instance of classical bridge prior art.

mechanisms.ambient_carrier: Lucas/quadratic-algebra carrier whose suitable prime-channel group order divides p+1 when the discriminant is a nonsquare modulo p
mechanisms.hidden_channel_invariant: Lucas rank/order controlled by p-(D/p), specializing to p+1 in the nonsquare channel
mechanisms.public_factor_blind_action: evaluate a Lucas-sequence multiple/index M modulo N using public parameters
mechanisms.collapse: standard Lucas identity value (schematically V_M=2) in one prime channel but not the other
mechanisms.endpoint_extraction: a gcd of the corresponding Lucas identity defect with N, schematically gcd(V_M-2,N)
mechanisms.crt_restatement: Exact under the standard Lucas nondegeneracy/discriminant hypotheses: if p divides the public Lucas identity defect and q does not, gcd(defect,N)=p. The p+1 smoothness route is therefore another one-sided hidden-channel order annihilation.
mechanisms.success_regime: A prime divisor p for which the relevant p+1/Lucas order is smooth enough for M, with no simultaneous collapse in the other channel; implementations have parameter and exceptional-case conditions.
mechanisms.cost_regime: Conditional on p+1/Lucas-order smoothness; no unconditional complexity theorem asserted here.
mechanisms.bridge_class: one-sided quadratic/Lucas order annihilation -> gcd endpoint
mechanisms.novelty_guard_effect: Changing from F_p^* to a quadratic/Lucas carrier is not by itself a new bridge family when annihilation and extraction remain equivalent.

mechanisms.ambient_carrier: random elliptic curve over Z/NZ, projecting to elliptic-curve groups E(F_p), E(F_q) when reductions are nonsingular
mechanisms.hidden_channel_invariant: random prime-channel group/order of the chosen point; #E(F_p) varies with the curve rather than being fixed at p-1
mechanisms.public_factor_blind_action: choose public/random curve and point, perform the same scalar multiplication [M]P modulo N
mechanisms.collapse: [M]P reaches the identity modulo p while the q-channel does not, manifested during composite-modulus arithmetic by a projective coordinate or denominator that is noninvertible modulo N
mechanisms.crt_restatement: Exact at the endpoint: a coordinate divisible by p but not q is a nonunit/zero-divisor witness and its gcd with N is p. The hidden asymmetry comes from different elliptic-curve group orders in the prime channels.
mechanisms.success_regime: A selected curve/point has sufficiently smooth order in a hidden prime channel; randomizing the curve randomizes the relevant group order.
mechanisms.cost_regime: Lenstra's original paper states a conjectural expected-time bound; this ledger does not promote that heuristic/conjectural complexity to an unconditional theorem.
mechanisms.bridge_class: one-sided random-group annihilation -> inversion failure/nonunit -> gcd endpoint
mechanisms.novelty_guard_effect: A new carrier with randomized hidden order but the same annihilation/nonunit/gcd endpoint pattern must clear ECM/cyclotomic equivalence before novelty is claimed.

mechanisms.ambient_carrier: iterated map on Z/NZ with hidden CRT projections to finite state spaces modulo p and q
mechanisms.hidden_channel_invariant: channel-specific orbit/cycle structure and collision time
mechanisms.public_factor_blind_action: iterate the same public polynomial/map modulo N
mechanisms.collapse: x_i=x_j mod p while x_i!=x_j mod q (or vice versa)
mechanisms.endpoint_extraction: gcd(x_i-x_j,N), often batched by a product of differences
mechanisms.crt_restatement: Exact: one-channel equality makes p divide x_i-x_j; failure of equality in the other channel keeps q from dividing it, so gcd recovers p.
mechanisms.success_regime: A useful collision occurs in one hidden channel before simultaneous collision destroys the distinguishing witness.
mechanisms.cost_regime: Pollard's original paper describes the method as apparently finding a prime factor p in O(sqrt(p)) arithmetic operations; this is recorded as the source's probabilistic/heuristic performance statement, not an unconditional deterministic bound.
mechanisms.bridge_class: one-sided collision -> difference nonunit -> gcd endpoint
mechanisms.novelty_guard_effect: Factor-blind dynamics plus hidden CRT collision asymmetry plus gcd extraction is classical and cannot support a new bridge-family claim by itself.

mechanisms.ambient_carrier: square classes/residue relations modulo N; practical algorithms construct relations in integer/factor-base spaces then project to Z/NZ
mechanisms.hidden_channel_invariant: CRT sign pattern of square roots: x=+/-y independently modulo each prime factor
mechanisms.public_factor_blind_action: construct a congruence x^2=y^2 mod N without knowing the factors
mechanisms.collapse: x=y in one prime channel and x=-y in another, rather than the globally trivial same-sign cases
mechanisms.crt_restatement: Exact for odd squarefree semiprime N=pq: a nontrivial congruence of squares with opposite hidden sign choices yields one prime from gcd(x-y,N) and the other from gcd(x+y,N). The subtraction is an equality detector in the residue ring, not an additive distance.
mechanisms.success_regime: Once a nontrivial congruence of squares is obtained, extraction is deterministic; relation-finding cost depends on the specific factoring algorithm (Dixon/QS/NFS-type variants).
mechanisms.cost_regime: No single asymptotic claim is attached to the whole family in this ledger; Pomerance's quadratic-sieve source is used as the representative classical mechanism reference.
mechanisms.bridge_class: hidden CRT sign split -> nontrivial square-root collision -> gcd endpoint
mechanisms.novelty_guard_effect: A candidate whose endpoint is merely a nontrivial congruence of squares followed by gcd belongs to a mature collision/sign-split bridge family.

mechanisms.ambient_carrier: cyclotomic/algebraic extension carriers constructed so an annihilating exponent is controlled by Phi_k(p)
mechanisms.hidden_channel_invariant: divisibility/order information attached to the kth cyclotomic polynomial Phi_k(p)
mechanisms.public_factor_blind_action: universal algebraic-number-theory construction driven by a supplied multiple of Phi_k(p)
mechanisms.collapse: one hidden prime channel is annihilated/singularized under the cyclotomic action before the other
mechanisms.endpoint_extraction: factor split through the construction's nonunit/gcd-type endpoint
mechanisms.crt_restatement: Mechanism-level: Bach-Shallit explicitly give a universal construction for Phi_k that subsumes prior p-1, p+1 and other low-degree cyclotomic methods. Therefore a higher-order carrier plus known order annihilation is not automatically a new bridge family.
mechanisms.success_regime: A suitable multiple E of Phi_k(p) is available; the paper's general expected-time statement is conditional on generalized Riemann hypotheses.
mechanisms.cost_regime: Record only the source's conditional/GRH expected-time scope; no unconditional inference is made here.
mechanisms.bridge_class: higher algebraic order annihilation -> factor split
mechanisms.novelty_guard_effect: Higher-rank or extension-carrier terminology must be tested against cyclotomic universal constructions before being called new.

mechanisms.ambient_carrier: Z/NZ or a finite algebra over it
mechanisms.hidden_channel_invariant: a public witness z is zero/nonunit in one prime channel but a unit/nonzero in another
mechanisms.public_factor_blind_action: any process that manufactures a public residue/coordinate/norm/resultant z without factor labels
mechanisms.collapse: z becomes a nontrivial zero-divisor/nonunit modulo N
mechanisms.endpoint_extraction: gcd(z,N) (or an equivalent norm/resultant followed by gcd)
mechanisms.crt_restatement: Exact for N=pq: z=0 mod p and z!=0 mod q implies gcd(z,N)=p, up to the symmetric case.
mechanisms.success_regime: Extraction is immediate once such a witness is publicly available; the hard part is producing it factor-blindly.
mechanisms.cost_regime: Endpoint gcd is efficient; witness-generation cost belongs to the upstream mechanism and is not erased by calling the endpoint a bridge.
mechanisms.novelty_guard_effect: Producing a new-looking witness but ending with the same nonunit/gcd extraction does not make the extraction law novel; novelty, if any, must live upstream in carrier dynamics or collapse generation.

brc_novelty_guard.name: BRC_NOVELTY_GUARD_V1
brc_novelty_guard.rule: A BRC-derived factorization-bridge claim is not a new bridge family if, after an efficiently computable representation change or action semiconjugacy preserving hidden prime projections, its collapse predicate and endpoint factor set reduce to a known order-annihilation, collision/sign-split, cyclotomic-annihilation, or nonunit/zero-divisor-gcd mechanism.
automatic_rejectors: hidden CRT channels behave differently alone
one channel reaches identity/order collapse while another does not
one channel collides while another does not
manufacture a nonunit/zero-divisor and apply gcd
use a higher algebraic/cyclotomic carrier with otherwise classical annihilation
rename a congruence-of-squares sign split as a bridge
required_novelty_survivors: an irreducible cross-channel/rank-two coupling not computably reducible to independent hidden-channel dynamics
a collapse invariant not reducible to smooth group order, Lucas/cyclotomic annihilation, ordinary collision/sign split, or generic nonunit formation
or an endpoint recovery law not equivalent to gcd/nonunit/norm/resultant extraction
and in an algorithmic claim, factor-blind observability plus a quantified success and total-cost analysis

classification_rule.EXACT_EQUIVALENT: efficient carrier isomorphism/conjugacy preserves hidden projections, public action, collapse event and endpoint factor set
classification_rule.MECHANISM_SUBSUMED: not literally conjugate but instantiates a known annihilation/collision/nonunit template with the same endpoint law
classification_rule.PARTIAL_OVERLAP: shares support/collapse structure but no endpoint reduction or factorization semantics has been shown
classification_rule.NOVELTY_GAP_NOT_REDUCED: at least one essential carrier/coupling, collapse invariant, or endpoint law survives all listed reductions; this label is a research gap, not a novelty theorem

current_cbrc_mapping.accepted_predicate_summary: For the accepted two-slot automorphism carrier, survivor membership is exactly det(A)=+/-1, D invertible mod 3, gcd(|a|,|d|)>1 and gcd(|b|,|c|)>1; support-splitting strata cover the survivor set.
current_cbrc_mapping.reason: This is an exact operator-survivor/support classifier. It does not, at its accepted scope, take a composite N=pq as public input, expose hidden p/q CRT channel dynamics, produce a one-sided nonunit/collision witness modulo N, or define a factor endpoint/cost law.
current_cbrc_mapping.novelty_ceiling: It may support a project-specific bridge-existence/survivor-classification theory. It cannot by itself support a claim of a new factor-blind factorization bridge, a new CRT-channel collapse algorithm, or a new endpoint extraction mechanism.
